business.about: Incorporated in 2010, Eternal Limited (previously Zomato Limited) is one of the leading online Food Service platforms in terms of the value of food sold. Its offerings include food delivery, dining-out services, Loyalty programs, and others. As of December 31, 2020, Eternal has established a strong footprint across 23 countries with 131,233 active food delivery restaurants, 161,637 active delivery partners, and an average monthly food order of 10.7 million customers. [1]
business.in_their_words: We've been aggressively investing in growth, and we are seeing good outcomes on certain investments that we've experimented with in the last few quarters, and they're paying off well.

results.read: Revenue +78% YoY; EBITDA margin expanded 136 bps YoY to 3%; PAT +92% YoY.

calls: Margins expanding: 2% latest vs -49% average of prior years
Working capital stretching: cash-conversion cycle -132 → 2 days in 3 years
Weak cash conversion: 5-yr operating cash flow is -0.05× reported profit
Free cash flow negative in 4 of the last 5 years

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: Jignanshu, we are at that steady state now where about 90-95% is 1P, and we don't expect any more incremental working capital change on that account, if that was your question.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: We've given overall guidance of 60% CAGR and that would obviously mean some reasonable store expansion, but we're not planning to give out any specific number guidance on that.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: Yes, it will not be 100%, but we are not guiding to a specific number.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: We've tried to give you the building blocks of what the 60% CAGR guidance is based upon.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: Even though we might see capex per store going up over the next few quarters, we don't expect net working capital to be beyond those 18 days that we had shared earlier, so that should remain within range and hence, as a consequence of that, the ROCE outcome should still be north of 40%.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: As of now, as we have mentioned, we expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY, is what our current sense on the market is.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: So, the reality is the current growth rate number, which is around 15%, but whether you give guidance of 10% or 20%, you will have no basis for that.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: It's a judgment call and in the last letter we did say that for this financial year, we're unlikely to be at 20%, and we're expecting a 15% sort of year-on-year growth.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: So, Aditya, we should expect growth to be around the current level of ~30% year-on- year.

items.speaker: Akshant Goyal
items.quote: So, I do expect the year-on-year growth to remain above 100% for the next one or two years at least.

items.speaker: Albinder Singh Dhindsa
items.quote: We believe that most of the profits and the high-quality profits that we can target, reside in maybe the top 40% of the targetable market.

items.speaker: Albinder Singh Dhindsa
items.quote: Currently our viewpoint is that our current geographical footprint helps us cover about 20% of the overall targetable retail market that we're looking at.
